title: Last Stone Weight
description: You are given an array of stone weights. Repeatedly choose the two heaviest stones and smash them together. If their weights are equal, both stones are destroyed. Otherwise, the lighter stone is destroyed and the heavier stone is replaced by the difference of their weights. Return the weight of the last remaining stone, or 0 if no stones remain.
inputFormat: Second line: n space-separated stone weights
outputFormat: Print the weight of the last remaining stone, or 0 if no stones remain.

examples.explanation: After repeatedly smashing the two largest stones, one stone of weight 1 remains.

title: Maximum Product of Two Elements
description: Given an integer array nums, select the two largest elements and return the value of (largest - 1) multiplied by (secondLargest - 1).

examples.explanation: The two largest values are 5 and 4, so the result is (5-1)*(4-1)=12.
The two largest values are both 5.

title: K Weakest Rows in a Matrix
description: Each row of a binary matrix contains soldiers represented by 1 followed by civilians represented by 0. A row is weaker if it has fewer soldiers. If two rows have the same number of soldiers, the row with the smaller index is weaker. Return the indices of the k weakest rows.
inputFormat: First line: integers rows, columns and k
Next rows lines: columns space-separated binary integers
outputFormat: Print the indices of the k weakest rows separated by spaces.
constraints: All 1 values appear before all 0 values in each row

examples.explanation: Rows 2, 0 and 3 are the three weakest rows.

title: Kth Largest Element
description: Given an unsorted integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array. The kth largest element is determined by sorted order, not by distinct values.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. Sort the result by decreasing frequency. If two elements have the same frequency, place the smaller value first.
outputFormat: Print the k most frequent elements separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: 1 appears three times and 2 appears twice.
All values have equal frequency, so smaller values come first.

title: K Closest Points to Origin
description: Given a list of two-dimensional points and an integer k, return the k points closest to the origin. Distance is compared using x*x + y*y. Sort the selected points by increasing distance, then by x-coordinate, and then by y-coordinate.
inputFormat: First line: integers n and k
Next n lines: integers x and y
outputFormat: Print one selected point per line as x y.

examples.explanation: The two closest points have squared distance 8.

title: Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
description: You are given ropes of different lengths. Connecting two ropes costs the sum of their lengths. The connected rope can be used again. Find the minimum total cost required to connect all ropes into one rope.
inputFormat: Second line: n space-separated rope lengths
outputFormat: Print the minimum total connection cost.

examples.explanation: Connect 2 and 3, then 4 and 5, and finally 6 and 9.

title: Merge K Sorted Arrays
description: Given k individually sorted arrays, merge them into one sorted array.
inputFormat: For each array: first an integer size followed by size sorted integers on the same line
outputFormat: Print all merged elements in sorted order separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: All values from the three sorted arrays are merged.

title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description: You are given k sorted integer lists. Find the smallest inclusive range [left, right] that contains at least one number from every list. If multiple ranges have the same length, return the one with the smaller left value.
inputFormat: For each list: first an integer size followed by size sorted integers on the same line
outputFormat: Print left and right separated by a space.

examples.explanation: The range [20,24] contains 24 from the first list, 20 from the second and 22 from the third.

title: Sliding Window Median
description: Given an integer array nums and a window size k, return the median of every contiguous window. Print every median with exactly five digits after the decimal point.
inputFormat: First line: integers n and k
outputFormat: Print the median of every window separated by spaces, with exactly five digits after the decimal point.

examples.explanation: The median is calculated independently for every window of size 3.
For an even window size, the median is the average of the two middle elements.
